node.title: Re: By the shine on my bald pate, I dislike this encoding stuff
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
In addition to the issue [poj] [id://1210305|pointed out] with reading from twice (my(@LINES) = reads all lines from the file, so $filedata would normally be empty), I just wanted to point out that the pattern eval {...}; if ($@) {...} [id://1153468|has issues] and that the pattern eval {...; 1} or do {...} or a module like [mod://Try::Tiny] is better. Also, nowadays lexical filehandles (open my $fh, ...) are generally preferred over bareword filehandles (open ORDERFILE, ...). (Update: The AM also made a good point that you appear to be decoding the data twice.)

Really, the best way to go is to know in advance what encoding your files are in, and then opening them with the appropriate encoding in open my $fh, '<:encoding(...)', $filename or die $!;

You may want to have a look at [https://www.joelonsoftware.com/2003/10/08/the-absolute-minimum-every-software-developer-absolutely-positively-must-know-about-unicode-and-character-sets-no-excuses/|The Absolute Minimum Every Software Developer Absolutely, Positively Must Know About Unicode and Character Sets (No Excuses!)]

If you are sure that your files can only ever be UTF-8 or "ANSI" (by which I'm going to assume you mean [wp://Windows-1252], but [id://1198128|see also]), then you could use the following to guess which of the two the file is encoded in, but be aware this may still get things wrong, e.g. if you also have files encoded in, say, Latin-1 or Latin-9 ([id://1198298|see also]) this may not throw an error because the those encodings are so similar to CP1252!

use warnings; use strict; use Encode qw/decode/; sub guess_utf8_cp1252 { # WARNING: Does NOT work for other encodings my ($fn) = @_; open my $fh, '<:raw', $fn or die "$fn: $!"; my $raw = do { local $/; <$fh> }; # slurp close $fh; my $decoded; eval { $decoded = decode('UTF-8', $raw, Encode::FB_CROAK ); 1} or eval { $decoded = decode('CP1252', $raw, Encode::FB_CROAK ); 1} or die "$fn: Could not decode"; return $decoded; }
